en: Dr. Fe del Mundo invented a bamboo incubator that uses warm water jars to safely maintain a premature baby's body temperature without electricity.
The Executive branch's Department of Health enforces the Clean Air Act to reduce harmful vehicle emissions and prevent childhood asthma.
National hero Jose Rizal used his medical training and strict antiseptic techniques to safely perform an eye surgery restoring his mother's vision.
Practicing Arnis, the national martial art, requires wearing padded headgear and chest protectors to prevent concussions and fractures during sparring.
Participating in the Ati-Atihan festival requires applying thick, hypoallergenic sunblock to prevent severe sunburns and heatstroke from outdoor dancing.
The constitutional right to health obligates local governments to build proper drainage systems that prevent stagnant water and reduce dengue breeding.
The Igorot people built stone-walled rice terraces with continuously flowing irrigation water to naturally suppress mosquito larvae and prevent malaria.
The Filipino value of bayanihan helps communities safely evacuate to higher ground and share elevated shelters during dangerous typhoon surges.
The national flower, sampaguita, contains essential oils with natural antibacterial properties that traditional healers use to prevent wound infections.
The Manila galleon trade introduced vitamin-rich sweet potatoes to the Philippines, historically preventing scurvy and malnutrition among coastal communities.
The Philippine Red Cross translates vital first-aid and CPR instructions into regional languages to ensure accurate emergency responses nationwide.
During the Pahiyas Festival, families must thoroughly dry decorative rice grains to prevent toxic aflatoxin mold growth before consumption.
